comment: /* Aftermath */  "Some in the media" names nobody. The cited sources identify who objected.
/* Near misses */ "Only" editorializes. The second quotation adds little.
/* Aftermath */ Attributed to NIST. A contested technical conclusion needs in-text attribution, and the impact damage was part of NIST's finding.
/* Crash */ [[WP:EDITORIAL]]. "In spite of these hindrances" frames the Port Authority's conduct rather than reporting it.
/* Near misses */ Unattributed inference presented as near-fact.
/* Hijacking */ Named the body. Also, "terrorizing" duplicates what the facts convey.
/* Boarding */ Attributed to 9/11 Commission. "Likely" assigned the inference to nobody.
/* Boarding */ [[WP:YESPOV]]. Previous text attributed an emotional state and a motive to two people who left no record of either.
"Suicide dive" unnecessarily dramatizes. The body covers the training detail.
"Usurp" carries editorial color and adds no information.
My understanding is that the word "murdered" is a legal conclusion, so "killed" would be a more appropriate term for an encyclopedia. I also referenced [[WP:LOADED]].
/* Near misses */ Deleted the word "quote," which was unnecessary because quotation marks are present.
/* Near misses */ the word "yelled" is confusing here, without context, and unless the sources specifically states "yelled", I've changed it for a more suitable word
/* Calls */ Remove images that don't add anything to the article
/* */ well yes. Surely this can go without saying?
